definition: Alias means a false name used in place of one's real one.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word alias. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know alias should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The fugitive rented rooms under a different alias in every town, paying cash so that no register could tie the names together.
A nickname is far milder than an alias — it is affectionate, public, and hides nothing; half the point of a nickname is that everyone knows exactly who it belongs to.
A pen name stops short of an alias: it screens an author's name as an open convention that publishers and readers are in on, while an alias is built so identity cannot be traced at all.

A pseudonym is a false name adopted openly, often by a writer or artist — readers know the pseudonym hides a legal name and accept the game. An alias exists to conceal identity itself: the whole point of an alias is that someone is hiding.

An assumed name is the law's neutral term for any name a person takes on, honest or otherwise — a business can register one openly. An alias is the shadier cousin: a false name whose job is to keep its owner from ever being traced.

The census showed him in Chicago; after that, nothing -- until a shoebox of letters revealed why.
